correctness.rationale: Time s=bt gives dY/ds=−Y+S and rates alpha,beta. The stationary generator equation in state 0 yields (n+beta)m_n^0=alpha(m_n^++m_n^-), and the state + equation yields the stated even recurrence. Constant 0-to-plus hazard makes this conditional rest-position law the stationary entrance law. Its even moments identify the independent beta product by compact support. Expanding the symmetric part of (1−Y)^(-alpha) and using the duplication identities gives the displayed hypergeometric series with Gauss excess 1; this proves integrability and the Gamma quotient. Each plus mark has probability min(1,(delta/(1−Y))^alpha), so the stationary mark rate per entrance p_delta is asymptotic to the quotient times delta^alpha. The independent first rest after each plus run bounds all conditional later mark probabilities by kappa_delta tending to zero with log(1/delta) kappa_delta tending to zero. The Doeblin argument works uniformly: a long rest places every coordinate near zero, then a minus run of duration in a fixed positive interval, with a sufficiently short final rest, sweeps a common interval with bounded Jacobian and density bounded below. Thus separated stationary mark blocks mix uniformly. For block length L of order p_delta^(-1/2), short-lag joint contributions are O(L p_delta log(1/delta) kappa_delta), and long-lag contributions O(L^2 p_delta^2), both o(L p_delta). Logarithmic gaps have vanishing omitted hit probability and can make interblock total-variation error o(p_delta^2). This proves the exponential index law; the lower bound (delta/2)^alpha on conditional success gives uniform integrability. Full cycles have independent finite-mean lengths 2/alpha+2/beta; the first marked index is a stopping time for completed cycles with survival to a given cycle depending only on earlier cycles. The strong law and Wald's identity therefore apply, with finite expected post-hit remainder by memorylessness. For a stationary-time start, the first future plus entry has a finite-mean wait and any earlier hit is an event of probability tending to zero (the path stays strictly inside the support on the finite initial segment). The same order-delta^(-alpha) bound on conditional remaining mean makes dropping such events negligible for the scaled expectation as well. An initial entrance law not already stationary can be coupled after logarithmic burn-in; the first-mark probability vanishes at fixed interior positions and later burn-in hazards are bounded by kappa_delta. Restoring physical time multiplies the normalized clock by b, reproducing b/pi at (1,1) and b/2 at (2,1). Hitting and maximum events with strict versus weak inequalities give the same continuous limit by a threshold sandwich, with z=0 following from interior support. The supplied verification files were read as evidence, not executed; their simulations do not prove the temporal law.
